Adult Blood-based EPIC Clock trained by elastic-net regression of chronological age on whole-blood EPIC methylation in 1,592 MoBa-START adults aged 19–59 years.
Training/testing comprised 13,505 normal-tissue samples; prenatal datasets were encoded relative to 40 gestational weeks.

facts.fact: cultured human cells
adult primary human fibroblast cultures (39 training samples, passages 10–20)

CellPopAge is an elastic-net DNA-methylation clock using 42 selected CpGs to predict passage-based age of serially cultured adult primary human fibroblast populations and screen compounds that decelerate this measure.
The predictor was developed in 875 LBC1936 older adults with mean age 70.
The cortical clock training samples span ages 1–108 years.
facts.locator: Results “Developing a novel DNAm clock for the human cortex”; Methods/sample description

facts.fact: Cortex-specific DNA-methylation chronological-age estimator trained by elastic net on 1,047 post-mortem cortical samples; its 347-CpG weighted score is back-transformed to years.
facts.locator: Abstract; Materials and methods, 'Cortex training and test datasets' and 'Cortical clock development'

facts.fact: adults aged 18–75 years (210 normal liver samples)

LiverClock is a liver tissue-specific chronological-age clock trained by lasso on age-associated CpGs identified after adjustment for five estimated liver cell fractions; unlike HepClock, it is not hepatocyte-specific.
WHI, FHS-JHU, and LBC were the initial training cohorts.
The reference cells came from 37 anonymous healthy adults; donor ages ranged from 19 to 59 years.
The packaged six-cell reference contains 600 CpG rows; the origin paper separately reports a preferred 450-CpG EPIC IDOL library.

review_scope_note: All 40 inputs were compared field-by-field with their evidence-ledger entries. Exact-DOI citation counts and observation dates were checked against the 2026-10-02 citation audit. Crossref exact-DOI lookups found no bibliographic mismatch; its bioRxiv record omits a container-title field, while the bioRxiv record itself confirms the venue and author list. Primary paper landing pages/XML were requested live; some publisher endpoints returned 403/429, recorded above where this limits a claim. Existing source snapshots remain the evidence basis for those inaccessible records.
